text:
The Islanders are 12-7-5 and in the Metropolitan hunt, and the reason starts in net. They have allowed 13 fewer goals than their chances against predict, the kind of margin that turns a 47.6% expected-goals team (expected goals measure the quality of chances) into a .600 points percentage. Our numbers say they have about 5.6 more points than their play has earned, and their playoff odds sit at 47%, a coin flip.

The story people are writing about most is Matthew Schaefer, the 19-year-old defenseman whose second season has come with headlines about honoring his late mother, Jennifer. On the ice, he and Logan Stanley have played more five-on-five minutes than any Islanders pair and own 56% of the chances. Casey Cizikas played his 1,000th NHL game, all of it with this franchise, and Mathew Barzal is back from injury and setting up goals again.

Up front, Bo Horvat's line with Kyle Palmieri and Simon Holmstrom is the engine at 58% of the chances, and Holmstrom just had a seven-game point streak. Victor Eklund is the hot one: seven points in ten, against 4.7 expected. Coach Pete DeBoer's line on him, posted by Stefen Rosner: "He's got ice in his veins." What we'd watch is whether the five-on-five play catches up to the record before the saves stop coming.
headline: Islanders keep finding points the chances don't promise
